summary: Obfuscated postinstall payload executed via Function() during npm install
details: scripts/postinstall.cjs contains a plausible config-scaffolder followed, after a long whitespace pad, by an IIFE that globalizes `require`, `module`, `__dirname`, and `__filename`, reconstructs an obfuscated string via a custom Fisher-Yates permutation keyed on hardcoded integers plus %/#0/#1 character substitutions, compiles it through `String.constructor` (Function), and unconditionally invokes it (`FfK(4547)`) during `npm install`. The wrapper places the obfuscated block on the same line as the scaffolder's closing `};` behind ~2 KB of spaces so a casual editor view shows only the benign top portion. The bundled entries dist/index.cjs, dist/reporter-entry.cjs, and dist/cli.cjs additionally combine `require('child_process')`, hardcoded POST calls, and `ping`-based network probes. The lifecycle script fires automatically on every install and executes attacker-controlled code with Node internals available to the payload.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
